title: MERGE-XAI-SYNC C-13 (ADOPT 01 §3 S6, MCP long-prefix admission) — the upstream 1.0.31 behavior: an MCP tool whose fully-qualified name exceeds the 256-byte cap is ADMITTED (the base DROPS it); and OUR M7 child_tool_projection passes it to spawned children (the ours-side shape that must survive the merge). The rig: a hermetic MCP stdio stub (smoke/redteam/fixtures/merge-xai/c-13-mcp/mcp-longprefix-stub.py — stdlib-only JSON-RPC newline-delimited; initialize + tools/list exposing ONE 300-char tool 'longprefix_tool_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx' on server 'mxai_longprefix'; tools/call echoes args.echo — a test-double fixture, NOT a harness extension) whose qualified name 'mxai_longprefix__<300>' = 317 bytes (>256 — the admission edge). SETUP IS OPERATOR-DRIVEN (not a step-machine driver gap): config_patch is scalar-only and CANNOT add [mcp_servers.mxai_longprefix] (command/args are lists) — the operator provisions the server in the LIVE config from the stub fixture before the cell runs (README runbook; the hermetic home inherits the live mcp_servers block); an UNPROVISIONED server = BLOCKED (the harness-class premise lp_ann 0-hits — the announcement never reaches the wire), never a silent FAIL. PARENT ARM (turn 1 = announcement baseline; turn 2 = the coverage turn): a REAL use_tool round-trip to the 317-byte FQ tool with echo MXAI-C13-ECHO (discriminating pins: the escaped-JSON 'tool_name' key + the escaped-JSON FQ name — the prompt's plain mention and the announcement text cannot satisfy them). CHILD ARM (the M7 half, same turn): the parent spawns a qwen3.8-27b child instructed to call the SAME long-prefix tool with echo MXAI-C13-CHILD and finish, then wait_agents and quotes the child's result. SCORED PINS: (1) lp_ann (HARNESS premise — BLOCKED if 0-hit): the announcement '- mxai_longprefix (' reached the wire (the rig offered the tool); (2) lp_call + lp_tgt (MODEL premises): the parent issued a use_tool targeting the FQ name; (3) child_tool_closed (MODEL premise): the child's qwen request carries a function_call_output (the child round-trip CLOSED on the >256 tool — a real execution, not an emission); (4) done: the parent's terminal carries MXAI-C13-CALLED; (5) child_longprefix_ok (MODEL premise — THE M7 VERDICT): the parent's terminal carries MXAI-C13-CHILD — the child USED the >256 tool = the child_tool_projection passed it (ours' M7 shape under the merge); absent = the upstream base drop landed in the projection (or the model didn't spawn — the premise pass sorts it; the wire record adjudicates). VERDICT: PASS = all pins green (long-prefix admission + child projection both verified); VACUOUS = the model didn't take the path; BLOCKED = the server never announced. STOP-AND-REPORT: an acp_error, a 400/503 on the MCP boundary, or a child request storm.

steps.prompt: Perform exactly these tool uses, in this order, and no other tools: (1) use the use_tool tool to call the MCP tool on server mxai_longprefix (qualified name mxai_longprefix__longprefix_tool_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx) with argument echo 'MXAI-C13-ECHO'; (2) use the spawn_agent tool to start a background agent named child with model qwen3.8-27b (pass model: qwen3.8-27b in the tool arguments) and give it this task: use the use_tool tool to call the MCP tool on server mxai_longprefix (qualified name mxai_longprefix__longprefix_tool_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx) with argument echo 'MXAI-C13-CHILD', and only then finish; (3) use wait_agent to wait for the child to finish. When the tool result and the child's result are both in hand, reply with exactly: MXAI-C13-CALLED <the tool result> CHILD-RESULT <the child's final reply>

steps.note: SETUP PROVENANCE (recon_note, non-scoring): the [mcp_servers.mxai_longprefix] server must be provisioned in the LIVE config by the operator before this cell runs (the stub fixture smoke/redteam/fixtures/merge-xai/c-13-mcp/ is the double; config_patch cannot add it — scalar-only; README runbook C-13). Unprovisioned = BLOCKED via lp_ann (harness-class), never a silent FAIL. The >256 admission edge: qualified name = 317 bytes ('mxai_longprefix__' = 17 + tool name = 300); the base DROPS tools past the 256 cap, upstream 1.0.31 ADMITS them — the parent arm scores the admission, the child arm scores the M7 child_tool_projection passing the admitted tool through (ours' shape). The echo nonces (MXAI-C13-ECHO parent / MXAI-C13-CHILD child) are the round-trip payload proof: the stub echoes args.echo verbatim, so a nonce in a terminal that the model never read from a tool result cannot be parroted from the prompt into a RESULT (the result pins are the function_call_output shapes + the reply payload pins together).

ndjson.label: SESSION SURVIVES THE MCP BOUNDARY: an unrecovered 400/503 on the parent or the child MCP boundary surfaces here (Fatal tail) -> STOP (house rule: new phrasing = triage).

PARENT ROUND-TRIP CLOSED: the parent's terminal carries the CALLED nonce — the use_tool call to the >256 tool was issued AND the result (the stub's echo) came back into the reply (the parent arm of the 1.0.31 admission claim).

M7 CHILD-PROJECTION VERDICT (the ours-side half): the parent's terminal carries the child's echo nonce — the CHILD used the >256 tool (its result flowed child -> parent via the mailbox/wait and was quoted). Present = the child_tool_projection PASSED the long-prefix tool through to the child (ours' M7 shape survived the merge under the upstream admission). Absent = the upstream base drop landed in the projection (the child could not call the tool) = defect — OR the model never spawned the child (the premise pass sorts it; the child_tool_closed wire record adjudicates: closed-but-no-echo = projection defect; never-closed = spawn/model problem).

wire.label: CONTROL (harness premise, BLOCKED if 0-hit): the mxai_longprefix MCP server's turn-boundary announcement ('MCP server(s) connected: - mxai_longprefix (1 tool): …') actually reached the lane's wire — the rig offered the long-prefix tool. 0-hit = the server was never provisioned/started (operator setup, README runbook C-13) = BLOCKED/HARNESS — no model or product conclusion is possible without the offer; NEVER a silent FAIL.

CONTROL (model premise, DISCRIMINATING FORM): a use_tool call was actually ISSUED — the escaped-JSON 'tool_name' key appears only in a real function_call's arguments (the responses wire JSON-encodes arguments as a string); the tools[] schema entry (single-level quotes) and the prompt (plain text) cannot match it. Only use_tool carries a tool_name parameter. 0-hit = VACUOUS (the model never called into MCP).

CONTROL (model premise, DISCRIMINATING FORM — THE >256 TARGET): a use_tool call targeted the DECLARED fully-qualified tool (the 317-byte FQ name in escaped-JSON form — the prompt carries the name plain without surrounding quotes, and the announcement lists the BARE tool name with no FQ prefix, so only a real call's arguments match). 0-hit = the parent never targeted the long-prefix tool (VACUOUS for the admission claim). HIT = the >256 name was ADMITTED onto the wire (the base would have DROPPED it — the 1.0.31 behavior under our code).

CHILD ROUND-TRIP CLOSED (model premise, the M7 half's wire face): a child (qwen) request carries a function_call_output item — the child's MCP call EXECUTED and its result was carried back into the child's context (proves execution on the child side, not merely emission). Combined with child_longprefix_ok (the child's echo in the parent's terminal): present+present = the child used the >256 tool (projection passed it); closed-but-echo-absent = the child ran a DIFFERENT tool or the echo was lost (adjudicate); absent = the child never closed a tool round-trip (spawn/model problem — the premise pass sorts it).
CHILD REQUEST BAND: 2-4 = the clean shape (spawn + task + tool round-trip turns); 1 = the child ran one request (adjudicate); >6 = storm -> STOP.

VERDICT RECORD (evidence-only, machine-readable): the upstream HTTP status of the LAST sol request (no status_in — a 400 on the MCP round-trip is a tool-path FINDING surfaced by the round-trip pins, and the session-title side call (same body.model, 500s proxy-side) may land last, so an assertive status_in would false-fail — the t21 status_rec convention).

vacuous_if.note: the mxai_longprefix server never announced on the lane wire — operator provisioning missing (README runbook C-13) or the stub failed to start; the rig failed, no model/product conclusion is possible. BLOCKED, never FAIL.

no use_tool call was issued on the lane (escaped 'tool_name' 0-hit — the tools[] schema presence of use_tool does NOT count) — the model did not take the MCP-call path; the admission probe is meaningless.
no use_tool call targeted the 317-byte FQ name (escaped-form 0-hit — the prompt's plain mention does NOT count) — the declared long-prefix target was never called; the admission probe is meaningless.

the child's echo nonce never reached the parent's terminal — the child did not use the >256 tool (model didn't spawn / child took a different path); the M7 projection verdict is uninterpretable (the child_tool_closed wire record adjudicates projection-defect vs spawn-problem on review).
